title: 只含受控源的单口：等效电阻可以为负
statement: 图示单口网络中 R_1 = 2 Ω，R_2 = 2 Ω，电流控制电流源 F 从结点 c 向下抽走电流 3i_1，i_1 是 R_1 中的电流（参考方向见图）。网络内部没有独立源。
求 a、b 端的戴维宁等效电路，并讨论结果的物理意义。

questions.explain: 端口开路时 i_1 = 0，受控源电流 3i_1 = 0，网络内没有任何激励，各处电压电流都为零：u_oc = 0。
外加电流 i_x 流入 a：i_1 = i_x，R_2 中电流 i_1 − 3i_1 = −2i_x，u = 2i_x + 2 × (−2i_x) = −2i_x，R_eq = −2 Ω。

choices: 端口电压与流入电流方向相反，网络实际向外部提供功率，能量来自受控源
计算一定有错，等效电阻不可能为负
该网络的开路电压为负
choiceExplain: 只含电阻的网络 R_eq 才不可能为负；含受控源（有源元件）的网络可以呈现负电阻。
开路电压 u_oc = 0（网络内无独立源）；负的是 u/i 之比 R_eq，不是开路电压。
questions.explain: 端口吸收的功率 u·i_x = −2i_x² < 0。受控源是有源元件，可以使端口呈现负电阻；只含电阻的网络才不可能。

questions.ask: 若在 a、b 间只接一个 2 Ω 电阻（不接任何电源），会怎样？
choices: 总电阻 R_eq + 2 = 0，电路方程没有唯一解（数学模型失效）
2 Ω = |R_eq|，满足最大功率匹配条件，电阻获得最大功率
choiceExplain: i = 0 只是 0·i = 0 的无穷多个解之一；总电阻为零时方程不能确定电流，模型已经失效，谈不上“一切正常”。
匹配条件 R_L = R_eq 只适用于 R_eq > 0 的含源网络，不能取 |R_eq|；而且这里 u_oc = 0，网络内没有独立源，本来就没有可传输的功率。
questions.explain: 回路方程变成 (R_eq + R)·i = 0·i = 0，i 可以取任意值：理想模型下解不唯一，实际电路会因非理想因素而不稳定。

hints: 没有独立源的网络，开路电压一定为零，戴维宁等效电路只剩一个电阻。
外加电源法：从 a 注入电流 i_x，则 i_1 = i_x；对结点 c 列 KCL 求 R_2 中的电流。
solution: **1. 开路电压。** 网络内无独立源，端口开路时 i_1 = 0 → 受控源电流为 0，整个网络零状态：**u_oc = 0**。
**2. 外加电源法。** 在 a、b 间外加电流 i_x（流入 a）。R_1 中 i_1 = i_x；结点 c 的 KCL：R_2 中向下的电流 = i_1 − 3i_1 = −2i_x。
**3. 等效电路：** 一个 −2 Ω 的电阻（u_oc = 0，没有电压源）。
**4. 物理意义：** 端口吸收功率 p = u·i_x = −2i_x² < 0，网络对外发出功率，能量由受控源提供（受控源吸收功率 = u_c·3i_x，u_c = −4i_x，为 −12i_x²）。

en.title: A one-port with only a dependent source: negative resistance
statement: In the one-port, R_1 = 2 Ω, R_2 = 2 Ω, and the current-controlled current source F draws a current 3i_1 downward out of node c, where i_1 is the current in R_1 (reference direction as drawn). There is no independent source inside.
Find the Thevenin equivalent at a, b and discuss the physical meaning of the result.

questions.explain: With the port open, i_1 = 0, so the dependent source current 3i_1 = 0; there is no excitation and every voltage and current is zero: u_oc = 0.
Drive a current i_x into a: i_1 = i_x, the current in R_2 is i_1 − 3i_1 = −2i_x, u = 2i_x + 2 × (−2i_x) = −2i_x, R_eq = −2 Ω.

choices: The port voltage is opposite to the entering current: the network actually delivers power, supplied by the dependent source
There must be a mistake: an equivalent resistance can't be negative
The open-circuit voltage of the network is negative
choiceExplain: Only a network of resistors alone can't have a negative R_eq; a network with a dependent source (an active element) can.
The open-circuit voltage is u_oc = 0 (there is no independent source inside); it is the ratio u/i, R_eq, that is negative.
questions.explain: The power absorbed at the port is u·i_x = −2i_x² < 0. A dependent source is an active element and can make a port look like a negative resistance; a network of resistors alone never can.

questions.ask: What happens if only a 2 Ω resistor (and no source) is connected across a, b?
choices: The total resistance R_eq + 2 = 0 and the circuit equation has no unique solution (the model breaks down)
The current is 0 and nothing special happens
2 Ω = |R_eq| meets the maximum-power matching condition, so the resistor receives maximum power
choiceExplain: i = 0 is only one of infinitely many solutions of 0·i = 0; with zero total resistance the equation can't fix the current, so the model has broken down — hardly "nothing special".

The matching condition R_L = R_eq applies to a network with R_eq > 0 and cannot be used with |R_eq|; besides, u_oc = 0 here and there is no independent source, so there is no power to transfer in the first place.
questions.explain: The loop equation becomes (R_eq + R)·i = 0·i = 0, satisfied by any i: the ideal model has no unique solution, and a real circuit would be unstable because of non-ideal effects.

hints: A network without independent sources always has zero open-circuit voltage: its Thevenin equivalent is just a resistor.
Test-source method: inject i_x into a, so i_1 = i_x; write KCL at node c to get the current in R_2.
solution: **1. Open-circuit voltage.** No independent source inside; with the port open i_1 = 0 → the dependent source current is 0 and the whole network is at rest: **u_oc = 0**.
**2. Test source.** Drive a current i_x into a. R_1 carries i_1 = i_x; KCL at c: the downward current in R_2 = i_1 − 3i_1 = −2i_x.
Port voltage u = R_1·i_1 + R_2·(−2i_x) = 2i_x − 4i_x = −2i_x → **R_eq = −2 Ω**.
**3. Equivalent circuit:** a single −2 Ω resistor (u_oc = 0, no voltage source).
**4. Physical meaning:** the port absorbs p = u·i_x = −2i_x² < 0, i.e. the network delivers power, supplied by the dependent source (it absorbs u_c·3i_x with u_c = −4i_x, i.e. −12i_x²).
